title: Test
summary: This lesson explores photosynthesis, the essential process by which plants convert sunlight into energy using chlorophyll, carbon dioxide, and water. Students will learn how plants produce glucose and oxygen to support life on Earth.

sections.text: Scene: A bright green plant leaf is shown absorbing bright sunlight, with visible green chlorophyll pigments capturing the light energy. I wonder...? Answer: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert sunlight into energy.

Scene: A colorful chemical diagram illustrates carbon dioxide and water entering the plant, transforming into glucose and oxygen. I wonder...? Answer: Plants use CO2 and water to produce glucose and oxygen.

Scene: A glowing diagram highlights how oxygen and food are distributed to support life across the Earth. I wonder...? Answer: This process is essential for life on Earth as it produces oxygen and food for plants.

learning_objectives: Understand how plants convert sunlight into energy through photosynthesis
Identify the inputs and outputs of the photosynthetic process
Explain why photosynthesis is essential for life on Earth

vocabulary.definition: The process by which plants convert sunlight into energy.
The substance that absorbs light energy in plants.
